evidence_status: Sourced evidence compiled 2026-08-24 from WHO/AAP/peer-reviewed literature; Gate O clinical sign-off by owner/reviewer still pending before launch marketing

handoff.target_customer: Mother or primary caregiver of a newborn (0-3 weeks), in Nigeria/Africa or the diaspora, responsible for daily umbilical stump care - often with conflicting advice from grandmothers, aunties and hospital staff about what to apply and what to avoid
handoff.approved_situation: The baby's umbilical stump is still attached and must be kept clean and dry while relatives insist on traditional substances (toothpaste, shea butter, herbs, hot compresses) and hospital discharge instructions said something different

current_behavior: Applying whatever substance the most senior relative recommends
Cleaning the stump with multiple antiseptics
Covering the stump with belly bands or coins
current_conditions: Substances applied on top of hospital instructions
No agreed household rule for who decides cord questions
emotional_state: Guilt and fear about causing infection
practical_consequences: Infection signs missed or over-reacted to
failed_attempts: Toothpaste, shea butter, methylated spirit layered together
Asking three different people and getting three answers
environmental_constraints: Home birth or early discharge common
Chlorhexidine gel not stocked in many pharmacies

new_capabilities: Can name which traditional substances are dangerous vs unnecessary
Runs a daily 30-second check with clear pass/fail criteria
improvements: Family conflict reduced by pre-agreed rules
systems_created: A written cord-care house rule everyone in the home follows
remaining_limits: Does not replace newborn wellness visits
evidence_of_change: Zero harmful substances applied after starting
Caregiver can state the five red flags unprompted
Timely clinic presentation when flags appear

handoff.mechanism: Replace conflicting folklore with ONE default (clean, dry, exposed) plus a decision tree that converts anxiety into observable criteria, and scripts that de-escalate family pressure without confrontation
key_actions: Establish the baseline: what is currently being applied, by whom, and why
Install ONE written household cord rule before opinions arrive
Execute clean-dry-exposed care with a 30-second daily check
Convert worry into triage using observable criteria
Handle separation event, granuloma awareness, delayed separation

first_win.action: Write the House Rule ('Nothing goes on the stump. Clean, dry, exposed.') on the fridge card and send the respect-script message to the two most influential relatives
first_win.observable_change: A posted rule exists and the household's next response to advice is the script, not an argument

failure_points.scenario: Grandmother applies toothpaste/sheabutter during a nap
failure_points.rescue_protocol: Do-not-blame reset script: clean gently with water, restate house rule, move stump-supplies out of reach; log the incident, watch 48h extra

failure_points.failure_type: stump looks 'wrong' but baby is well
failure_points.scenario: Yellowish crusting or mild smell causes panic at midnight
failure_points.rescue_protocol: Decision tree normal/worry branches; if no red flags, continue routine and re-check in 12h; document photo for clinic

failure_points.scenario: Spreading redness, pus, fever >=38C or lethargy
failure_points.rescue_protocol: Rescue card: same-day medical care - emergency numbers per region; do not apply anything else to the stump
Book medical review; note whether dry or moist; no pulling, twisting, or home removal attempts

failure_points.scenario: New helper arrives week two with fresh advice
failure_points.rescue_protocol: Handover card: new helper reads the one-page house rule before touching baby care duties

before_baseline: Number of substances applied to stump in last 48h
Household disagreement events about cord care
success_indicators: Zero harmful substances applied from Day 1 to separation
All red-flag events resulted in same-day care
Zero major family conflicts over cord care
tsm.success_threshold: 60%+ of completers meet >=3 of 4 indicators at Day 30 review
tsm.measurement_method: Self-reported daily log + structured Day-30 check-in against baseline
tsm.incomplete_progress_interpretation: Partial adherence is expected during family pressure spikes; only harmful-substance exposure resets progress to Day 1 of run phase
tsm.next_action_on_miss: Re-run the Diagnose stage with the specific person who applied substances; install handover card for helpers

maintenance.maintenance_system: After separation: weekly navel check inside bath routine until fully healed
maintenance.relapse_protocol: If any substance is applied again post-separation due to rash/bleeding worries: stop, photograph, route through decision tree rather than home treatment
maintenance.reentry_protocol: Restart at Stage 3 (routine) with whoever now performs baby care; no guilt reset
